set.seed(42)
alpha <- 0.05
k <- 3  # repeated measurements
mu1 <- 51
mu2 <- 49
sigma_marginal <- 2.5
rho <- 0.5
n_per_group <- 18
num_simulations <- 10000

cat("Monte Carlo Verification\n")
cat("========================\n\n")
cat(sprintf("Simulating %d studies, each with n = %d per group\n", num_simulations, n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Repeated measurements: k = %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Compound symmetry correlation: ρ = %.2f\n\n", rho))

# Create compound symmetry correlation structure
# Correlation matrix for k measurements within a subject
corr_matrix <- matrix(rho, nrow = k, ncol = k)
diag(corr_matrix) <- 1

# Convert to covariance matrix with marginal SD = sigma_marginal
cov_matrix <- corr_matrix * sigma_marginal^2

# Vector of means for subject-level average over measurements
mean_vector_g1 <- rep(mu1, k)
mean_vector_g2 <- rep(mu2, k)

# Simulate studies
rejected <- 0

for (sim in 1:num_simulations) {
  # Group 1: n participants, k measurements each
  group1_data <- mvrnorm(n = n_per_group, mu = mean_vector_g1, Sigma = cov_matrix)
  
  # Group 2: n participants, k measurements each
  group2_data <- mvrnorm(n = n_per_group, mu = mean_vector_g2, Sigma = cov_matrix)
  
  # Compute subject-level averages
  group1_avgs <- rowMeans(group1_data)
  group2_avgs <- rowMeans(group2_data)
  
  # Perform two-sample t-test on subject-level averages
  t_test_result <- t.test(group1_avgs, group2_avgs, var.equal = TRUE)
  
  # Check if reject null hypothesis
  if (t_test_result$p.value < alpha) {
    rejected <- rejected + 1
  }
}

monte_carlo_se <- sqrt(simulated_power * (1 - simulated_power) / num_simulations)
ci_lower <- simulated_power - 1.96 * monte_carlo_se
ci_upper <- simulated_power + 1.96 * monte_carlo_se

cat(sprintf("Null hypothesis rejections: %d / %d\n", rejected, num_simulations))
cat(sprintf("Simulated power: %.6f\n", simulated_power))

# where n is participants per group

# Using the noncentral t distribution:
# For balanced two-sample t-test:
# df = 2n - 2 (total n_total = 2n)
# λ = δ * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(|t_{2n-2}| > t_{α/2, 2n-2}) under λ
#       = P(t_{2n-2,λ} > t_{α/2, 2n-2}) + P(t_{2n-2,λ} < -t_{α/2, 2n-2})

# Critical value for two-sided test

# Function to compute power given n per group
compute_power_ttest <- function(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  se_diff <- sd_avg * sqrt(2 / n)  # SE of difference of means
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  lambda <- delta / se_diff  # noncentrality parameter
  
  # Power = P(|t| > t_crit) under noncentral t
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + (1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda))
  return(power)
}

# Create compound symmetry correlation structure
# Correlation matrix for k measurements within a subject
corr_matrix <- matrix(rho, nrow = k, ncol = k)
diag(corr_matrix) <- 1

# Convert to covariance matrix with marginal SD = sigma_marginal
cov_matrix <- corr_matrix * sigma_marginal^2

# Vector of means for subject-level average over measurements
mean_vector_g1 <- rep(mu1, k)
mean_vector_g2 <- rep(mu2, k)

# Simulate studies
rejected <- 0

for (sim in 1:num_simulations) {
  # Group 1: n participants, k measurements each
  group1_data <- mvrnorm(n = n_per_group, mu = mean_vector_g1, Sigma = cov_matrix)
  
  # Group 2: n participants, k measurements each
  group2_data <- mvrnorm(n = n_per_group, mu = mean_vector_g2, Sigma = cov_matrix)
  
  # Compute subject-level averages
  group1_avgs <- rowMeans(group1_data)
  group2_avgs <- rowMeans(group2_data)
  
  # Perform two-sample t-test on subject-level averages
  t_test_result <- t.test(group1_avgs, group2_avgs, var.equal = TRUE)
  
  # Check if reject null hypothesis
  if (t_test_result$p.value < alpha) {

  }
}
